claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Abstract only: a UCB exploration strategy perturbs a SIMP-based, DfAM-constrained TO model across compliance and thermal-conduction problems to generate diverse designs; the abstract claims improved computational scalability versus data-reliant deep-learning TO methods, without a quantitative classical-method comparison.
claim.key_phrase: fulfills a gap in computationally efficient methods for exploring generative designs
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable: full text is not accessible (see version_coded). The abstract gives no timing figure, speedup factor, or explicit quantitative comparison to a classical (non-learned) TO run; it states only a general claim of improved 'scalability to real-world and often computationally expensive part design applications' relative to 'other data-reliant deep learning methods used in TO.'
claim.alternatives: None identifiable without full text; the abstract does not name specific alternative candidate primary outcomes.

baseline.classical_method: Solid Isotropic Material Penalization (SIMP)-based density topology optimization, perturbed via an Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) exploration parameter, with support-minimization and thin-feature-minimization Design-for-Additive-Manufacturing (DfAM) filters (per the abstract); further detail not available
baseline.training_time: Described in the abstract as a 'non-data-driven learning method ... based on historical TO iterations,' contrasted with 'data-reliant deep learning methods used in TO,' suggesting no separate offline training dataset, but no cost figure of any kind is given
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated (abstract only; the abstract's own framing suggests this method is not data-driven, but gives no cost figure)
